penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise ITSM migration decisions are high-stakes, multi-stakeholder processes; buyers at this level expect live discovery calls, workshops, and presentations — async-only delivery won't close.

penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Migration planning and cost analysis for ServiceNow environments requires bespoke analysis of the customer's contract, architecture, and org context — not automatable via a generic Claude pipeline.

rationale: The pain is real and the dollar amounts are large — multi-million dollar renewals under renegotiation — but the buyer is an enterprise IT/procurement team that cannot be sold to asynchronously or at scale by a solo operator. Reaching and closing enterprise buyers requires live engagement (calls, RFPs, procurement cycles), and the analysis work is inherently bespoke per customer. Operational autonomy scores 3 because every deliverable would require Youval's direct involvement; this is consulting, not a product.
solution_plan: This is not a viable solo factory build. The opportunity is real at the enterprise level, but enterprise ITSM migration advisory is a professional services engagement — it requires discovery calls to understand each company's ServiceNow configuration, custom cost modeling, and stakeholder presentations. None of that can be automated by Claude + a landing page. A lighter version (e.g. a self-serve 'ServiceNow self-host cost estimator' tool) could be explored as a lead-gen asset, but on its own it would not generate meaningful revenue without the consulting engagement behind it, which is beyond the factory's model.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (3, min 7). Signal worth monitoring — if a lightweight SaaS ITSM alternative emerges as the framing, rescope and re-score.
